html:
The constitution of Ghana's Fourth Republic, approved by referendum in April 1992 and in force from January 1993.

It set up a president limited to two terms, a parliament and independent courts after decades of coups. Since then power has passed peacefully between the two main parties, the National Democratic Congress founded by Jerry Rawlings and the New Patriotic Party, in 2000, 2008, 2016 and 2024, including after a close result decided by the Supreme Court in 2013. Ghana is often held up as a model of democracy in West Africa. See also the 1966 coup and Nkrumah.
sum: The constitution of Ghana's Fourth Republic, approved by referendum in April 1992 and in force from January 1993.
